cities.d: (Ulan Bator, Mongolian: Улаанбаатар) – the capital city and starting point for most travel in this country. Half the population lives here.

x.around: Street names are rarely known by Mongolians, and they usually only appear on maps and official addresses. Official addresses list the district, microdistrict (usually a large block bounded by major streets), and the building number. However, since blocks can have dozens of buildings, with more continuously being squeezed in between existing ones, addresses are not very helpful for navigation.
x.intro: Ulaanbaatar (Улаанбаатар) — also Ulan Bator, UB, or in the local language, Khot ("the city") — is the capital and the largest city of Mongolia. With more than 1.6 million residents as of 2023, Ulaanbaatar is home to roughly half of Mongolia's population and serves as the starting point for pretty much all travel around Mongolia.

must.d: The main monastery in the city has services around 10:00 every morning. It is one of the few monasteries in the country that were spared during the Communist purges of the 1930s.

The big open space in the center of the city with an equestrian statue of Damdin Sükhbaatar, warrior-hero of the 1921 People's Revolution, as well as a seated statue of Genghis Khan that sits at the door of the Government Palace.

These five temples and five arched gates are a unique showcase of religious art and the history of Buddhism in Mongolia, a gem of 20th century Mongolian cultural heritage, and a fine example of Buddhist architecture.

This museum holds the most important artifacts of Mongolia's rich history dating back several thousand years. These include ethnographic displays of various Mongolian tribes, petroglyphs and cave drawings, Turkic monuments,…

Built between 1893 and 1903 by Mongolian masters, this palace was dedicated to the VIII Bogd Gegeen, head of Tibetan Buddhism and Khan of Mongolia from 1911 until 1924 (the last three years of which were as a constitutional…

n.es: Palacio de Invierno del Bogd Khan

must.d: The complete fossil of the Tarbosaurus bataar — a close cousin of the larger T. Rex that serves as the centerpiece of this museum's impressive collection — was stolen from Mongolia by American archaeologist Eric Prokopi and…

n.es: Museo de historia natural de Mongolia

must.d: A huge Communist-era monument on a hill near the city depicting the Russian and Mongolian heroes who fought together during the First and Second World Wars.
Mongolia's national public broadcaster, operating television and radio services. The headquarters houses its main studios and broadcasting facilities.

next.d: scenic, forested mountain valleys a mere three-hour bus ride from UB
the ancient capital of the Mongol Empire in the beautiful Orkhon River valley, a day's bus ride to the west
nomadic camel herders and dinosaur fossils
where the old Kazakh tradition of eagle-hunting lives on in the snow-capped Altai Mountains

x.safe: While crime rates in Ulaanbaatar are said to be among the highest of any Asian city, this generally applies less to the city center than the underdeveloped ger districts on the outskirts of town: poorly lit shantytowns crisscrossed by maze-like dirt alleys and row upon row of fences; not the kind of place most tourists would be interested in to begin with.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Чойбалсан) – large industrial city in the east

hidden.d: Natural history/ethnography museum, Mongolian warrior monument, tank, etc, including tributes to Soviet general Georgy Zhukov, who quashed the Imperial Japanese Army during the Battle of Khalkin Gol that took place nearby.

Nice place to relax and take in some fresh air. Concrete esplanade extends all the way to the Herlen River (~1-2 km) if you really feel like getting a walk in and feel the -20 degree Celsius Siberian burn.

x.intro: Choibalsan (Mongolian: Чойбалсан) is the capital of Dornod province and the fourth-largest city in Mongolia. The name of the city was Bayan Tu'men (Баян Түмэн) until 1941, when it was renamed after the communist leader Khorloogiin Choibalsan. The city administrative unit's official name is Kherlen sum, with area of 281 km2. It is situated at the Kherlen River, at an elevation of 747 m above sea level.

next.d: in Inner Mongolia, China, which is more than 400 km east of Choibalsan.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Эрдэнэт) – Mongolia's second largest city and home to one of the world's biggest copper mines and a famous carpet factory

x.intro: Erdenet, with a population of nearly 89,000, is the second largest city in Mongolia and capital of Orhon province. Erdenet is 375 km away from Ulaanbaatar city.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Ховд) – a historic city at the crossroads of traditional Mongol and Kazakh culture

x.around: Transportation within Khovd Aimag - You can get a car, furgon (a 4×4 UAZ van) or jeep in the market to get around the aimag and to neighboring aimags. - Vehicles (jeeps/cars/pargons) for soums leave from two different places near the central market. The first is along the main road in front of the north entrance to the central market. The second is along the road behind the central market.
x.intro: Jyrgalant is the capital of the Hovd province of Mongolia. By extension it is directly named Khovd or Hovd (Mongolian: Ховд). It has a population of around 30,000. Note that there is a different village close to it that has this name.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Хархорум) – the ancient capital of the Mongol Empire, established by Genghis' son Ogedei

hidden.d: Cultural center
Anyone who's interested in steppe history and/or the history of the Turkic peoples should visit Khar Balgas, the ancient capital of the Uighur Khaganate.
Run-of-river dam along Orkhon River.
Art gallery

x.intro: For other destinations with the name "Karakorum", see Karakoram. Karakorum (also spelled Kharahhorin, Karakorin, Karakorum, and Kharkhorin) is a city in Central Mongolia, about 300 km west of Ulaanbaatar as the crow flies. Locals call it Har Horin or Harhorin.

must.d: The capital is located on the north side of the Erdene Zuu Monastery. Go to the northwest corner of the Monastery, enter the fenced compound, used to be a sign here stating that the UN had paid for the fence.
This monastery was built in the 1500s, but has been destroyed several times. It is free to enter the grounds, but a tour inside the old temples costs 3000 ₮, 5000 more to take pictures inside.
Southwest on the west side of the river to the bridge at N46 48.503 E102 1.668. Cross to the south side and continue west to the falls.
Go southwest from Harhorin on the west bank of the Orhon River to N46 56.000 E102 22.322 turn right (west) There is a park entrance with US$3 fee per person.
Art center specialized in creating and preserving traditional Mongolia script calligraphy. Exhibition halls are placed inside various ger.

x.safe: When driving in Kharkhorin, always be alert for any crossing horses or cows at all time. When walking along the sidewalks of the city, be aware for any animal feces, mainly from horses and cows.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Мөрөн) – a stopover for those visiting Hövsgöl province, it has several museums and a large collection of deer stones outside of town

x.around: The town is small enough to walk around. From the town there is the biggest fresh water lake Lake Khövsgöl located 100km to the north that is main attraction in the province.
x.intro: Mörön is the capital of Hövsgöl in Northern Mongolia, and a usual stopover en route due to its central location in the province.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Өлгий) – a town in Mongolia's far western corner, the starting point for visiting Altai Tavan Bogd National Park, Tsambagarav National Park and the eagle hunters who live

x.around: Ölgii is not a large town so you should be able to get most places by walking, 30-40 minutes at the most. There are no addresses. Business cards usually provide directions from a nearby landmark. For example, an office might be "2nd floor of Altai Cashmere Building next to Post Office." Unofficial taxis are cheap and can be found alongside major roads or in/near the city square.

hidden.d: This giant red building was constructed to promote Kazakh culture and host events in the city and now has concerts and plays from locals and groups traveling from Kazakhstan or elsewhere in Mongolia.

Family-owned and -operated travel company that has extensive experience with foreigners and U.S. Peace Corps volunteers. Offers packaged trips to Tavan Bogd National Park, fishing trips, and other custom packages.

Bear Valley has tour packages that offer cultural experiences, trekking, hiking, horseback-riding, fishing, cycling, kayaking, and mountain climbing. The owner, Akhmaral, has been a guide for many years.
They offer a broad selection of tour packages and services, including scheduled shuttle services to Tavan Bogd and unguided tours.
It is a nice place to hang out in the evenings; has cheap beer and soft drinks, and is one of the greener spots in town.

They provide fishing, bird watching, mountain biking, hiking, horseback riding, jeep, hiking, whitewater rafting, and mountain climbing. The owner, Bekbolat, is an expert mountain climber and whitewater rafting guide.

x.intro: Ölgii is the capital of Bayan-Ölgii province and is also known as Olgii, Ulgy, or Ulgii. Ölgii serves as the starting off point for visiting Altai Tavan Bogd National Park and Tsambagarav National Park and the beautiful snow-capped mountains, glaciers, plentiful wildlife, nomadic herders who live in felt tents called gers, and eagle hunters just outside the city.

must.d: It's worth going on hikes up into the nearby mountains; find someone familiar who can guide you there, or just walk in any directions. Bugan Tou Mountain to the southwest can be hiked at 2775 m.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Чингис) – near the birthplace (and possible burial site) of Genghis Khan

x.around: Ondorkhaan is aligned along a southwest-northeast axis, and is about 5 km long. Most travel is done by walking, but taxis are common. There is a taxi stand in front of the West Market. Also, just standing beside the road and stretching your arm will flag a taxi. The rate is 500 ₮/km.

hidden.d: Located in a single-story building with a yellow roof
This is the centrally located city park in Ondorkhaan. It starts at the Museum of Khentii and ends at the sports complex. There are a few monuments and tanks from the Soviet era.
An art workspace with exhibitions.

This is the premiere museum in Khentii. As of 2018 it is closed for repairs, which show no sign of activity or progress. It used to be open from Tuesday-Saturday 09:00-18:00 and cost about US$1 per person.
The renovated Buddhist Monastery (surrounded by large white walls). It is an impressive structure and one of the most beautiful places in Khentii.

x.intro: Ondorkhaan (also spelled Öndörkhaan and Undur Khan, Mongolian: Өндөрхаан) is a city in Eastern Mongolia. It was renamed Chinggis City (Чингис) in 2013 to honor the great conqueror born in the north of the province. Government sources (including maps and buses) will generally use the new name, however Mongolians are more likely to know it by the old one, and using the old name for internet searches helps avoid the many other conflicting uses of the name "Chinggis".
x.safe: There are pick-pockets (including children), primarily in the markets and the main shopping district. Also, beware of drunk people and avoid them.

cities.d: (Mongolian: Цэцэрлэг) – the most pleasant of Mongolia's provincial capitals sits in a beautiful forested valley in the Khangay mountains

x.around: Tseterleg isn't very big. The city center and most hotels are in walking distance of the main attractions. If you don't want to walk, stand on the side of the road and stick your hand out. It won't be long before a car stops. Expect to pay between 500 and 2,000 ₮ for rides around town.

hidden.d: the town's main monastery

n.en: Bronze Age Complex Site with Deer Stones at Jargalantyn Am (JA) – 1st protected area
Bronze Age complex Site with Deer Stones at Khoid Tamir

hidden.d: The ARA Festival happens every summer during the whole month of July. Concerts, shows, food, horse races, activities for the whole family. It's all located in the ARA complex, 10 minutes by car from the center.
Formerly Zayain Khüree Monastery, has local artifacts and displays.

n.en: Bronze Age Complex Site with Deer Stones at Jargalantyn Am (JA) – 2nd protected area

x.intro: Tsetserleg (also spelt Tsetserlik, Tsetserlig or Cècèrlèg) is the capital of Arkhangai province. The town is located in a beautiful forested valley in the Khangay mountains; it has a population of around 20,000, and is generally considered to be the most pleasant of Mongolia's provincial capitals.

intro: Mongolia (Mongolian: Монгол улс, Traditional Mongolian: ) has wide open spaces for experiencing the outdoors for those who want adventure. Its vast and majestic emptiness is the country's enduring appeal: it brings the traveller into a close communion with nature and its nomadic inhabitants. It is one of the last places on earth where nomadic life lives on. The most memorable part of a trip to Mongolia will be its hospitable people.

other.d: (Mongolian Cyrillic: Алтай Таван богд байгалийн цогцолбор газар) — the tallest mountain and largest glacier in Mongolia, with Kazakh Eagle Hunters living in its shadow and a World Heritage Site:…

n.it: parco nazionale di Altai Tavan Bogd

hidden.d: The twin lakes of Khoton Nuur and Khurgan Nuur and nearby Dayan Nuur has most of the people and archeology of the park, as well as the greenest scenery. Kazakh nomads live on the shores of the lakes during the summer.
The White River is the main valley flowing from the Tavan Bogd Mountains to Tsengel village and the center section of the UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The mountains present a stunning view, with a 2,000-m massif and snow covered peaks. Below the peak is the 23-km² Potuniin Glacier and many more smaller glaciers and peaks.

River flows from the main mountain passes south of Tavan Bogd Mountains into Khoton Nuur and then Kurgan Nuur and the Hovd River. This forested valley has an abundance of wildlife and various monuments.
Hiking, trekking and photography tours in western Mongolia. Offers all inclusive packages to custom-made tours Mongolia.

White Valley is also called Baga Oigor, lies at the northern edge of the park close to the Russian border and is the largest concentration of petroglyphs, stone men, and burial mounds in all of Central Asia.

x.intro: Altai Tavan Bogd National Park (Mongolian: Алтай Таван богд байгалийн цогцолбор газар) is located on the westernmost point of Mongolia in Bayan-Ulgii Province. This vast mountainous park borders China and Russia with views of Kazakhstan from the highest peak in Mongolia.

next.d: the capital of Bayan-Ölgii Aimag (province) and center of Kazakh culture in Mongolia.
on the other side of Bayan-Ölgii, has the 2nd-highest mountain in Mongolia and lots of wildlife, and Uriankhai and Kazakh nomads living inside the park.
in Russia is right across the border with dense forests and the snow-capped Golden Mountains of Altai.
covers the Chinese side of the mountains, though travelling there will require a tour guide and visa beforehand.

x.safe: When traveling in the park, especially if you're an individual or an independent group, it's best to register with the park office and let them know your intentions. There is no "rescue" service of any kind in Mongolia, but at least they'll know where to begin looking for you if you do go missing or get hurt.

other.d: (Mongolian Cyrillic: Увс нуур), Uvs province — the largest lake in Mongolia and a World Heritage Site: Uvs Lake
(Mongolian Cyrillic: Горхи-Тэрэлж) — a national park 70 km east of Ulaanbaatar

hidden.d: Bridge crossing, flying fox, rock climbing

Completed in 2004, the temple is often mistaken for the "Princess Temple."A total of 108 stone steps lead up to the temple, and the surrounding area features 108 small stupas, 8 religious offerings, and a metal fence adorned with…
It is a giant rock that looks like a turtle.

x.intro: Gorkhi-Terelj National Park (Горхи-Тэрэлж) is in Tuv of Mongolia, 55 km outside of Ulaanbaatar. It's one of Mongolia's top attractions.

other.d: (Mongolian Cyrillic: Хөвсгөл нуур) — a large freshwater alpine lake

x.intro: Lake Khövsgöl is the largest freshwater lake in Mongolia by volume. It is near the northern border of Mongolia, about 200 km (124 mi) west of the southern end of Lake Baikal.
x.safe: The lake is located in the big permafrost zone. Swimming is mostly impossible. Perhaps, with insulated diving suit, one can swim and dive.

other.d: (Mongolian Cyrillic: Дархадын хотгор) — home to the Reindeer people
(Mongolian: Хустайн нуруу) — Khustain Nuruu or Hustai National Park is home to the Takhi wild horses (also known as Przewalski's Horse). These are true wild horses which have never been domesticated.

x.intro: Khustain Nuruu National Park, also known as Hustai National Park, is in the Tuv Aimag of Mongolia.

other.d: (Mongolian Cyrillic: Говь гурван сайхан байгалийн цогцолбор газар) — Khongor Sand dunes, Yol Canyon, Bayanzag-Red Flaming Cliffs, and Khermen Tsav

x.intro: Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park is in the central part of Gobi region, in southern Mongolia. The place has many sand dunes but with sparse vegetations which is much different than other deserts of the world.
